title: Key Allocation Contention in Relational Key Tables
pattern: Managing unique key generation by maintaining a single row per table in a relational database, and locking that row (`FOR UPDATE`) for every insert.
why_bad: High lock contention. Every concurrent insert transaction must serialize on this single row lock, killing parallel write performance and rendering multi-core database scaling useless [308, 313].
detection: SQL statements executing `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on tables with schema structures like `(table_name, next_id)`.
counterexample: Key tables using block-reservation patterns (e.g., Hi-Lo algorithm) where a block of IDs is reserved at once.
fix: Reserve a batch of IDs (e.g., increment by 100) using a single query to reduce database calls and eliminate lock contention.
